newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Parana ports handle 18 million tonnes cargo in 96.
newsitem.headline: Parana ports handle 18 million tonnes cargo in 96.

text.p: The Brazilian port of Paranagua and its auxiliary Antonina handled a total of 18.35 million tonnes of products for import and export in 1996, up around seven percent on the previous year, the ports' authority said.

Soybeans and soymeal accounted for the largest part with a combined total of 8.63 million tonnes loaded. Paranagua, located in the key soybean producing region of Parana, is the largest terminal in South America for loading grains, the port authority said in a report.
But vegetable oil loading levels fell from 1995, despite a rise in the production of Brazilian soybeans. Loadings totalled 804,139 tonnes, down from 997,062 tonnes the previous year.
The smaller port of Antonina handled 720,652 tonnes in 1996. This was up more than 1,500 percent on the previous year following the installation of two private terminals.

Jose Anibal Petraglia, superintendent of the port administration authority, said Paranagua was aiming to handle 30 million tonnes per year. Most of the increase was seen coming from the general cargo sector.
